knowledge:
- key_parameters: fq=Path to the input FASTQ file containing sequencing reads ;; ref=The reference sequence string or path to a FASTA file of the target region ;; cutsite=The position of the gene-editing cut site within the reference sequence ;; allele_table=A data frame containing the allele profiles generated by IndelForm
- alternatives: Cassiopeia (for large-scale single-cell lineage tracing), DCAL, or AMELIE. Prefer LinTInd for standard amplicon-based scar tracing with integrated visualization of indel alignments and trees.
- when_to_use: Use when you have amplicon sequencing data from CRISPR/Cas9-based lineage tracing experiments and want to identify scars (indels) to reconstruct cell lineage trees.
- pitfalls: Ensure the cutsite parameter is accurately specified relative to the reference sequence, as incorrect cutsite coordinates will lead to wrong indel definitions. High sequencing error rates can be mistaken for true indels; pre-filtering reads is highly recommended.

workflows.name: lineage_reconstruction
workflows.intent: Reconstruct a lineage tree and visualize indel patterns from CRISPR-edited amplicon sequencing data.
input: reads.fastq (FASTQ file containing amplicon sequencing reads of the edited target region)
reference.fasta (FASTA file containing the unedited reference sequence of the target region)
workflows.stages: 1. Identify indels from sequencing reads using FindIndel() ;; 2. Generate allele profiles from identified indels using IndelForm() ;; 3. Reconstruct the lineage tree using BuildTree() ;; 4. Visualize the reconstructed lineage tree using PlotTree() ;; 5. Plot the indel alignment patterns using IndelPlot()
workflows.code:
library(LinTInd)
indels <- FindIndel(fq = "reads.fastq", ref = "reference.fasta", cutsite = 17)
allele_table <- IndelForm(indels)
tree <- BuildTree(allele_table)
PlotTree(tree)
IndelPlot(allele_table)
